newsitem.title: USA: Washington Water files for Idaho rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Washington Water files for Idaho rate cut.

text.p: Washington Water Power on Thursday said it has filed for a rate reduction in Idaho that would decrease the average customers electric utility rate by 2.427 percent.

The proposed rate cut, in the form of a power cost adjustment (PCA) rebate, was filed with the Idaho Public Utilities Commission. If approved, the rebate would be effective June 1, 1997 and expire May 31, 1998.
A typical Idaho residential customer using 1,020 kilowatt hours of electricity per month would see a monthly bill decrease of about $1.16, the company said in a statement.

The proposed rebate comes in addition to a current rebate that began September 1, 1996 and runs through August 31, 1997. Together, the two programs would cut rates by 4.771 percent, or $2.27 in the average monthly bill of a customer using 1,020 kilowatt-hours of electricity.
